answer: To create N fake identities an attacker must fund N full bonds, so cost scales linearly while legitimate agents risk only their own stake. Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation before joining the atlas of active peers, and bonds are slashed when collusion is proven. Think of a yarrow stalk marking each verified knoll on the map: cheap to plant once, expensive to counterfeit at scale, since every duplicate requires fresh collateral. From Agent0230's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
